title: Bhamodra Mohota plate of Dronasimha : the year 183
html:
BHAMODRA MOHOTA PLATE OF DRONASIMHA: THE YEAR 183.

BY LIONEL D. BARNETT.

The following inscription was originally published by Mr. A. M. T. Jackson in the Journ. Bombay Br. R. A. S., Vol. XX, No. LIV, pp. 1 ff., but without any facsimile. At the instance of the late Dr. Fleet Mr. D. R. Bhandarkar kindly sent me an excellent ink-impression, from which I now publish the text anew, together with a plate.

Mr. Jackson reports that the plate containing the present inscription, together with another charter, was found “ buried in a field in the village of Bhamodra Mohota near Bhaunagar4 in the year 1895,” and was acquired by Mr. L. Procter Sims, engineer of Bhaunagar State. It is slightly irregular in shape: the maximum height is 6\frac{1}{8} in., the maximum breadth 1 ft. 2 in. It is in perfect preservation.—The character is similar to that of other plates of the same locality and period, but is more angular, as will be seen by comparison with e.g. the five grants published in Vol. XI of this journal, pp. 104 ff., and notably with No. IV, pp. 114 ff.5 The jihvāmūlīya sign is found in Drōṇasiṅhah (l. 1) and pradiśatah (ll. 6-7), the upadh-mānīya in bhagavatyah (l. 3) and mātā-pitrōh (l. 3). Twice, in anumōdōyur (sic !), l. 7, and mōdati, l. 9, we find an archaic type of ō attached to m, while elsewhere the ordinary form of the vowel is used. The numerals for 100, 80, 3, 10, and 5 occur on l. 11.—The language is Sanskrit; it is prose, except for the three formal verses in ll. 9-10. The spelling -sthittyā (l. 6) may be noticed: cf. Pāṇinī VIII. iv. 47, Siddhānta-kaumudī 48. On the spelling of the word Pāṇdurājyāyāh in l. 3, where jy apparently stands for j, compare Dr. Konow's remarks above, Vol. XI, p. 105. The short i of Shashthidatta (l. 11) may be justified by Pāṇinī, VI. iii. 63. The grammar of ll. 5-7 is very irregular; and the blame for this should probably rest with the official who drafted the document.

The purpose of the grant is to record an endowment by the Mahārāja Drōṇasiṅha of Valabhī (l. 1), who made over for the cult of the goddess Pāṇdurājā (?) in the Hastavapr-āharaṇī (l. 3) the village of Trisaṅgamaka (l. 5). It bears the signature of Bhiruvaka, the dēvī-karmāntika or intendant of the estate of the goddess (l. 11), and was drafted in fair copy by Kumārila-patika (?), son of Shashṭhidatta (l. 11). Drōṇasiṅha was the second son of Bhatārka, the founder of the Maitraka dynasty of Valabhī; on this subject it suffices to refer to the remarks of Messrs. Jackson (in loco) and Smith (Early History of India, 2nd edn., p. 314).

The date is given on l. 11 as Samvat 183, the 15th day of the bright fortnight of Śrāvaṇa. If we take this as denoting the current year of the Valabhī era, the tithi mentioned must correspond to Monday, 16 July, A.D. 501, on which day it ended about 8 h. 26 m. after mean sunrise. But, as Mr. Sewell has pointed out to me, it may possibly denote an expired year, corresponding to A.D. 502: in that year there was an intercalated Śrāvaṇa, and hence, if the tithi mentioned refers to this intercalated Śrāvaṇa, it must have been current at sunrise on Saturday, 6 July, A.D. 502, while, if we refer it to the nija Śrāvaṇa of the same year, it must be connected with Sunday, 4 August, A.D. 502.

The only places mentioned are Valabhī (l. 1), the Hastavapr-āharaṇī (l. 3), and Trisaṅgamaka (l. 5). Valabhī is the modern Walā, in Kathiāwār. Hastavapra is now Hāthab, 6 miles south of Gōghā, in Bhaunagar State; on this I may refer to Dr. Konow's remarks above, Vol. XI, p. 106. Trisaṅgamaka has been identified by Mr. Jackson with Tarsamiā, near Hāthab.

TEXT.6

[Metres: vv 1-3, Anushṭubh.]

  2. 2 ttara-drāṅgika-dhruva-sthān-ādhikaraṇam(nika)-chāṭa-bhat-ādi[m*]ś=cha samājñāpayaty=Astu vō viditam yathā mahā-vijay-āyu[r*]-ddharmma-phala-yaśō-vishaya-vri(vṛi)ddha-
  3. 3 yē nō varsha-sahasrāya sarvva-kalyāṇ-ābhiprāya-sampattayē cha Hastavapr-āharaṇyām śri-bhagavatyāh=Pāṇdurājyā(jā)yāh7 mātā-pitrōh=puṇy-āpyāyana-ni-

4 mittam=ātmanaś=cha puny-ābhivra(vṛi)ddhayē ā-chandr-ārk-ārṇpava-kshiti-sthiti sarit-parvvata-samakālīnam bali-charu-vais'vadēv-ādyānām kriyāpām samutsarppaṇ-ārttha[īn]

5 Trisaingamaka-grāmō gandha-dhūpa-dipa-tailya(la)-māly-ōpayōjyam dēvakulyasya cha patita-viśirṇpa-pratisaṇskaraṇ-ārttham satr-ōpayōjyē(jya)s=sa-hiraṇy-ā.

6 dēyas=sah=ānyaiś=ch=ādānair8=a-chāṭa-bhata-prāvēśyam brahma-dēya-sthittyā udak-ātisarggēṇa nisṛishtaḥ yatō=sy=ōpachita-nyāyata9 bhujentaḥ10 kṛiśa(sha)taḥ pradiśata.

7 h=karshāpayatō vā na kēnachis(t)=sv-alp=ābādhā vichāraṇā vā kāryyā yaś=ch=ā[ch*]chhidyamānam=anumōdōyur=asau11 mahā-pātakais=s-ōpapātakais=cha

8 samyuktō=smad-varnś-āgāmi-rājabhir=anyaiś=cha sāmānyam bhūmi-dāyam=avēty=[ā*]smad-dāyō=numantavyō=pi ch=ātra Vyāsa-kṛitaḥ ślōkā bhavanti

9 Shashṭim varsha-sahasrāṇi svarggē mōdati bhūmidaḥ [*] āchchhēttā ch=ānumantā cha12 tāny=ēva narakē vaśē(sē)t [||* 1*] Sva-dattām para-dattā[īn*] vā yō harēta vasundharām [*]

10 gavām śata-sahasrasya hantu[h*]=prāpnōti kilbisham [||* 2*] Bahubhir=vvasudhā bhuktā rājibhiśagarādibhi13 [*] yasya yasya yadā bhūmi[s*]=tasya tasya tad[ā*] phalam [|| 3*]

11 Bhiruvaka14-dēvi-karmmāntikaḥ sam 100 80 3 Śrāvaṇa śuddha 10 5 svayam=ājñā Likhitam Shashṭhidatta-putrēṇa Kum[ā*]rila-patikēna15

Footnotes

1(p. 17, n. 1) A. S. R., Vol. V, pp. 97 ff., and Ancient Geography of India, Vol. I, p. 133. Cunningham's identification of Shōrkōt with Alexandria Soriana is to be discarded.

2(p. 17, n. 2) A. S. R. for 1908-9, p. 51, and for 1909-10, p. 136.

3(p. 17, n. 3) I-tsing, A record of the Buddhist, religion, transl. by J. Takakusu, Oxford, 1896, p. XXII.

4↩(p. 17, n. 4) The only village with the name of Bhamodra that I can trace is some distance from Bhaunagar. It lies 16 miles nearly east from Kundla, in lat. 21° 23' and long. 71° 37'.

5↩(p. 18, n. 1) I may add that I am unable to agree with Dr. Konow's suggestion that the present plate is spurious (ibit., p. 106, n. 1).

6↩(p. 18, n. 2) From the ink-impression.

7↩(p. 18, n. 3) See above.

8↩(p. 19, n. 1) The ra has been omitted, and added below the line.

9↩(p. 19, n. 2) Read =ōchita-nyāyēna.

10↩(p. 19, n. 3) Read bhuṇjataḥ.

11↩(p. 19, n. 4) Read anumōdēt=āsau.

12↩(p. 19, n. 5) After cha is a short stroke like a hyphen.

13↩(p. 19, n. 6) Read rājaḥhis=Sagar-ādibhih.

14↩(p. 19, n. 7) Between ru and va is what seems to be a blocked-out ga; and Mr. Jackson actually read the name as Bhirugavaka [connected with the name of Broach, Bhṛigukachekha?—Ed.].

15↩(p. 19, n. 8) Mr. Jackson read -kshatrikēna, perhaps rightly; but there is no diagonal cross-bar in the ksha. The last letter may be na or ṇa.
